co-01.text: This is coffee I roasted myself this morning, in a popcorn popper, in twelve minutes.

co-02.text: By the end of this video you will have roasted your first batch, and you will have a one page checklist to do it again.

c1-01.text: You need three things, and you probably own two of them.

c1-02.text: A hot air popcorn popper, a metal colander, and green coffee beans.

c1-03.text: A second hand popper costs about $25, which is less than two bags of good beans.

c1-04.text: Do this next to an open window, because roasting makes smoke and the smell stays in the room.

c1-05.text: Measure half a cup of green beans. The popper needs room for the beans to spin.

c2-01.text: Switch the popper on, pour the beans in, and start a timer.

c2-02.text: For the first three minutes the beans turn from green to yellow and smell like hay.

c2-03.text: Around minute five you will hear a sharp pop. That sound is called first crack, and it means the beans are now coffee.

c2-04.text: From here you are choosing a flavour. Stop one minute after first crack for a light roast.

c2-05.text: Wait three minutes for a darker one. I think two minutes is the easiest place to start.

c2-06.text: Write the time down. That number is the only thing you change next week.

c3-01.text: Now the part people skip. Tip the beans into the colander and shake them by the window.

c3-02.text: They keep cooking until they are cool, so move fast. You want them warm to the touch in two minutes.

c3-03.text: Put them in a jar and leave the lid loose for a day, because fresh beans give off gas.

c3-04.text: Brew them tomorrow, not today. Rested coffee tastes sweeter.

c3-05.text: The checklist with every step and my roast times is free in the community, linked below. Come and post your first batch.
